intro: Salespeople build negotiation, persuasion and social perceptiveness skills that managers, brokers and marketers rely on. Of the 25 careers below, Advertising Sales Agents match salespeople most closely at 83%, and Sales Managers follow at 79% with a BLS May 2025 median of $148,270.
why_it_works: Sales trains you to read buyers, handle objections and close deals under a quota. O*NET rates negotiation, persuasion and social perceptiveness at 3.75 out of 5 for sales representatives, which is why management, real estate, fundraising and purchasing roles rank high. Purchasing managers use the same negotiation from the other side of the table. Marketing managers turn your customer insight into strategy. The main gaps are systems analysis and managing budgets and people.
tips: Aim for management if pay is the goal: sales, marketing and purchasing managers more than double the sales rep median.
Show results in numbers, such as quota attainment and account growth, because hiring managers in every match look for them.
Check licensing first for real estate, insurance and securities roles, since each needs its own state or industry license.

faq.q: What jobs can salespeople do besides sales?
faq.a: The closest matches are Advertising Sales Agents (83%), Sales Managers (79%) and Sales Engineers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Outside direct selling, Fundraisers (73%), Purchasing Managers (73%) and Logisticians (71%) use the same negotiation and relationship skills.

faq.q: Which careers pay more than sales?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more than the $72,080 median for wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (+131%), Sales Managers earn $148,270 (+106%) and Purchasing Managers earn $148,080 (+105%), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do salespeople need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Not for the options on this page: all 25 matches usually need no more education than a sales representative has, based on O*NET Job Zones. Management roles still favor a bachelor's degree, and 71% of Sales Managers report one as their education.

faq.q: What skills should salespeople build for a new career?
faq.a: Across the top 10 matches, the skills that most often need work are systems analysis, systems evaluation, managing financial resources and managing people. Your strongest skills, negotiation and persuasion, already rate 3.75 out of 5 in O*NET, so the gap is mostly in planning and leadership.
